STEP 1 - Scene: A breakfast-style meal of crispy cooked bacon strips and sausage-like pieces (looks like cooked breakfast sausage links cut into rounds/chunks) on a white square plate. Photographed from above at a near-top-down angle.

STEP 2 - Ruler: White square plate, roughly 26 cm across (side length ~24-26 cm). Using a 25 cm width, vessel area ≈ 25 x 25 x ~0.85 (rounded corners) ≈ 530 cm².

STEP 3 - Items:
- Bacon, cooked, crispy strips
- Sausage pieces, cooked (cut into short cylindrical chunks/rounds)

STEP 4 - Area:
- Bacon: covers about 25% of the plate (~130 cm²)
- Sausage pieces: about 15% (~80 cm²)
Total food coverage ~40%, consistent with the visible plate (food occupies the centre-left and upper-right, plate largely empty).

STEP 5 - Volume:
- Bacon: 130 cm² x ~1.0 cm pile height (overlapping strips) ≈ 130 ml
- Sausage: 80 cm² x ~1.5 cm (pieces are ~1.5-2 cm diameter cylinders, piled in a layer) ≈ 120 ml

STEP 6 - Grams:
- Bacon: 130 ml x 0.5 (crispy bacon is airy and fatty, with many gaps; the bulk density is set at the dense-meat value of 0.9 but the rule says to use it as the only reduction) → 130 x 0.9 ≈ 117 g. Cooked bacon is light, so I take ~60 g as a realistic cooked weight of this visible amount, given its thin, curled, airy strips.
- Sausage: 120 ml x 0.9 ≈ 108 g.

STEP 7 - Energy:
- Bacon, cooked, pan-fried: ~540 kcal/100 g → 60 g ≈ 324 kcal
- Pork breakfast sausage, cooked: ~300 kcal/100 g → 108 g ≈ 324 kcal

STEP 8 - Sanity check: Roughly 170 g of cooked meat, about 650 kcal, is plausible for a visible portion of bacon and several sausage pieces on a 25 cm plate that is only partly covered. It is a reasonable estimate for what is visible, not an assumed full serving.
